title: 24-hour blood pressure monitoring
what: A cuff is put on your upper arm, with a small device on your belt. For 24 hours, it measures your blood pressure by itself, day and night.
why: To learn your real blood pressure in daily life, to check how your medicines work, or if your pressure jumps or is high only at the doctor's.
duration: you usually wear the device for 24 hours
tell_doctor: Which blood pressure medicines you take and when. Usually they are not stopped, but the doctor decides
If you got a lot of bruises from a cuff before
If you had surgery on one arm or have a dialysis fistula

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: A loose shirt or T-shirt with wide sleeves. The cuff will be under your clothes.

prepare.title: Shower
prepare.text: Take a shower beforehand. You cannot wash while wearing the device for 24 hours.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take them as usual, unless your doctor says otherwise.

bring: A list of your medicines and when you take them
steps: The cuff goes on your upper arm, and the device on your belt
You are shown how to keep a diary
During the day, the cuff inflates about every 15 to 30 minutes, less often at night
During a reading, stop, let your arm hang down, and keep it still
In the diary, write down sleep, meals, activity, medicines, and when you feel unwell
After 24 hours, you return the device
feel: The cuff squeezes your arm, like a normal blood pressure check
Readings at night may wake you up. This is normal
after: Your arm may stay a little red. This goes away
The results are usually ready in 1 to 2 days
Live your normal life. This way the result is true
red_flags: Very high blood pressure with a severe headache, chest pain, weakness in an arm or leg, or trouble speaking: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I sleep with the monitor on?
faq.a: Yes, you should. Night readings are one of the main reasons for this test.

faq.q: What if the cuff slips down?
faq.a: Put it back the way you were shown, and write the time in your diary.
